findings.title: CVE-2026-42271 Detail (NVD entry)
findings.summary_md: NVD published the CVE-2026-42271 record on May 8, 2026: LiteLLM versions 1.74.2 through before 1.83.7 let any authenticated user, including holders of low-privilege internal-user keys, run arbitrary commands on the proxy host via the POST /mcp-rest/test/connection and POST /mcp-rest/test/tools/list endpoints, which pass the stdio command field to subprocess execution with no role check. GitHub rates it CVSS-B 8.7 High, CWE-77 and CWE-78, patched in 1.83.7. NVD also lists Red Hat OpenShift AI 2.25 before 2.25.8 and 3.3 before 3.3.4 as affected, with Red Hat errata referencing the CVE.

findings.title: BerriAI LiteLLM Command Injection Vulnerability (CISA KEV entry)
findings.summary_md: CISA added the BerriAI LiteLLM Command Injection Vulnerability, CVE-2026-42271, to the Known Exploited Vulnerabilities Catalog on June 8, 2026, with a federal remediation due date of June 22, 2026 under BOD 22-01. The KEV listing documents confirmed in-the-wild exploitation roughly eleven weeks before the Wiz honeypot research reached the news coverage in this story.

findings.title: GHSA-7488-6r32-c95q: MCP Authentication Bypass via OAuth2 Passthrough Fallback
findings.summary_md: BerriAI published GHSA-7488-6r32-c95q for CVE-2026-59822 on June 30, 2026, credited to GitHub user yaaras. A failed LiteLLM key validation falls back to an empty UserAPIKeyAuth() object, letting a fabricated Authorization header with any Bearer token, even a single character, establish an authenticated MCP session and reach configured MCP tooling. CVSS v4 is 8.8 High, all versions below 1.84.0 are affected, the fix is 1.84.0, and the stated workaround is disabling MCP routes or blocking /mcp/ at the reverse proxy or API gateway.

findings.title: Inside 90 days of attacks on AI infrastructure (Wiz Threat Research)
findings.summary_md: Wiz Threat Research published the underlying advisory on August 27, 2026, one day ahead of the cyberpress.org coverage in this story. It documents 90 days of honeypot telemetry across LiteLLM, Flowise, LangChain, Langflow, ChromaDB, and Ollama, including exploitation of CVE-2026-59822 and CVE-2026-42271, master key extraction from Python module memory, XMRig staging at /usr/src/node-red/xmrig, a miner hidden as unicorn under /app/data/.claude/ on the Langflow honeypot, and an external researcher link between the Qilin ransomware group and a CVE-2026-42271 plus CVE-2026-48710 Starlette host header chain. The full IoC set adds pool.hashvault[.]pro, crazyeltonproxy[.]top, 94.26.106[.]29, and 1710.rwlp.be to the two IPs the news story carries, plus default master key sk-1234 abuse and a State of AI in the Cloud finding that 90 percent of cloud environments run self-hosted AI software.
